_README: TOPICAL TEMPLATE — Stage 2 scoped fact-build for 3 domains ABSENT from the standard facts-template.json (health/pharmacy/hospital billing, Balearic ferries, public holidays/closures).

locale.money_framing: express costs in USD with EUR equivalents

_fact_field_shape: Every FACT uses: { value, source_url, status (verified|agreed_stable|verify_recommended|serve_live), notes }.

prescription_medication_rules.value: General Schengen practice: carry only a personal supply for the length of the trip, in original labeled packaging, plus a copy of the prescription or a doctor's letter naming the generic (INN) drug name — brand names differ by country. No single published day-count limit for tourists that I can confirm confidently.
prescription_medication_rules.notes: Day-count / quantity threshold NOT confirmed against an official source — leave verify_recommended, do not present a number as fact

controlled_substances_note.value: Narcotic/psychotropic medications (opioids, many benzodiazepines, and notably stimulant ADHD meds like Adderall — amphetamine salts are controlled and NOT approved for sale in Spain) require a 'Schengen certificate' for stays under 30 days, issued by the traveler's home-country competent authority, to legally carry them across a Schengen border. This is a genuine risk point for Americans specifically because Adderall is a common US prescription with no direct Spanish equivalent.
controlled_substances_note.notes: HIGH-STAKES for this audience — verify against Spain's AEMPS or the Schengen certificate official text before publishing

customs_declaration_threshold.notes: No confirmed threshold — leave null rather than guess

official_source_url.notes: AEMPS (Agencia Española de Medicamentos) or the US Embassy Madrid 'Medical' page are the likely official sources — need the panel/user to confirm the exact URL

farmacia_identification.value: Green cross sign (often lit and animated at night); ubiquitous even in small neighborhoods

farmacia_de_guardia.value: A rotating duty-pharmacy system keeps at least one pharmacy open 24h per zone even on nights/Sundays/holidays; the current on-duty pharmacy is posted in the window of every closed pharmacy and listed online (Barcelona's pharmacists' college, COFB, runs a farmacias de guardia lookup)
farmacia_de_guardia.notes: confirm the exact current lookup URL/tool before publishing

otc_vs_prescription_differences.value: Spain is somewhat more permissive at the pharmacist's discretion than the US for some items (e.g. the morning-after pill is sold OTC to adults without a prescription); conversely some US OTC staples may require asking the pharmacist by symptom rather than brand name since US brand names don't exist there

pharmacist_role.value: Spanish pharmacists are trained to diagnose and treat minor ailments directly at the counter (colds, minor wounds, rashes) and are a legitimate first stop before a clinic

private_clinic_access.value: Private walk-in clinics accept cash/card pay without an appointment; a straightforward consultation is a same-day, hours-not-days wait
private_clinic_access.notes: cost range NOT filled here — belongs in typical_costs as serve_live

public_hospital_er_access.value: Public hospital urgencias (ER) will treat any emergency regardless of ability to pay or nationality — emergency stabilization cannot legally be refused — but a US tourist is NOT covered by Spain's public system the way an EU resident is, so billing follows afterward for non-emergency-classified care

when_to_choose_which.value: Pharmacy first for anything minor; a private clinic for a non-urgent issue that still needs a doctor (better speed, English more likely, bill goes to travel insurance); public ER (or 112) only for a true emergency

billing_model_public.value: Non-EU tourists are generally billed for public hospital care beyond emergency stabilization; billing can happen at discharge or by mailed invoice afterward depending on the hospital
billing_model_public.notes: mechanism (discharge vs mailed invoice) not confirmed — real variation by hospital, needs a source

billing_model_private.value: Private hospitals/clinics typically ask for a card guarantee or upfront payment before non-emergency treatment, then the patient files for reimbursement with their own travel insurer

typical_costs.value: Rough, unverified order of magnitude only: a private walk-in consultation roughly $80-150; an ER visit/workup somewhat more; an ambulance ride and any overnight stay materially more — DO NOT publish these numbers as fact, they need a real source or should stay qualitative
typical_costs.notes: Flagging low confidence explicitly — this is the field most likely to need panel/human correction

travel_insurance_necessity.value: Essential, not optional, for this audience — US health insurance and Medicare do not cover care in Spain

what_to_keep_for_reimbursement.value: Itemized invoice (factura desglosada), the medical report (informe médico), and all payment receipts — a US insurer's claim form will ask for all three

operators.notes: the two main operators running Barcelona-Balearics; GNV also runs some Mediterranean routes but I'm not confident it covers Barcelona-Balearics specifically — verify

port_terminal.value: Port de Barcelona, near Drassanes/Barceloneta — Trasmediterránea uses the Moll de Barcelona / Terminal Drassanes/Ferry area, reachable by metro L3 (Drassanes) plus a short walk or port shuttle bus
port_terminal.notes: exact current terminal assignment per operator needs a live check

to_palma_mallorca.value: Historically an overnight slow ferry of roughly 7-8h with cabins is the mainstay; a faster daytime option in the 4.5-5h range has existed seasonally on some operators
to_palma_mallorca.notes: LOW CONFIDENCE — durations/existence of the fast option must be verified against the current operator timetable before writing

to_ibiza.value: Typically an overnight ferry in the roughly 8-9h range; I am not confident a same-day fast ferry exists on this specific leg

to_menorca.value: Often routed via Mallorca rather than direct, and more seasonal (summer-only) than the Ibiza/Mallorca legs
to_menorca.notes: LOW CONFIDENCE — verify direct vs routed and seasonality

fast_vs_slow_tradeoffs.value: Slow overnight ferry: cheaper per berth, you sleep through the crossing and arrive rested with a full day ahead, but you're committed to a cabin booking; fast ferry: burns a travel day but frees the evening — pick fast only if the schedule and price both work out, since it isn't always offered

booking_advice.value: Book weeks ahead for July-August sailings, earlier still if bringing a car; compare both the operator's own site and an aggregator (e.g. Direct Ferries) since fares/schedules aren't always mirrored

typical_causes.value: High wind and rough sea state are the recurring cause, most common in the shoulder/winter months but possible any time

passenger_rights.value: EU Regulation (EC) No 1177/2010 on the rights of passengers when traveling by sea and inland waterway governs assistance, rerouting, and compensation for cancelled/delayed EU ferry services
passenger_rights.notes: confirm the regulation number/current text and how it's applied in practice by these two operators

operator_rebooking_practice.notes: not confirmed — needs the panel or a real source

travel_insurance_interaction.value: A standard travel-insurance policy's 'trip interruption'/'common carrier delay' clause is what would cover a missed onward connection caused by a cancelled ferry — plain trip-cancellation coverage usually does not

national_holidays.notes: the fixed Spain-wide set; moderate-high confidence on the list, but yearly official gazette confirmation is the correct source

value.name: Dilluns de Pasqua Florida (Easter Monday)
value.typical_date: movable — observed in Catalonia though not nationally

value.name: Sant Esteve (St Stephen's Day / Boxing Day)

catalonia_regional_holidays.notes: Catalonia picks its own subset within the national 14-day cap — this list is my best general recall, NOT verified against the current year's official Generalitat calendar

barcelona_local_holidays.notes: Barcelona city council designates 2 local holidays per year and the second one varies/rotates — I could NOT confidently name the second one, left out rather than guessed. Santa Eulàlia (Feb 12) is a major festival but I'm not certain it's an official non-working local holiday vs. just a festival — flag for the panel

what_typically_closes.value: On the bigger national/religious holidays: most independent shops close, malls and big chains often stay open, restaurants (especially in tourist zones) mostly stay open, banks and post offices close, museums commonly run a Sunday-style schedule rather than closing outright, and public transport switches to its reduced Sunday/holiday timetable

august_shutdown_specifics.value: Many small, family-run businesses and neighborhood restaurants post 'cerrado por vacaciones' and close for one to a few weeks sometime in July-August, with no single fixed date across the city; tourist-center restaurants, hotels, major attractions, and chains stay open throughout
august_shutdown_specifics.notes: the general shape is well known; I can't confirm a specific percentage or exact typical window — needs either a source or should stay qualitative

advance_planning_note.value: Book sit-down dinner reservations further ahead around these dates, and double-check any specific restaurant/attraction's hours for the exact day rather than assuming normal hours

_open_questions._note: Genuinely unsure / needs a real source before publishing.
value: Medication import: no confirmed quantity/day-count threshold for personal prescription supply — needs an official source (AEMPS or embassy guidance)
Adderall/controlled-substance import: Schengen certificate requirement needs verification against the current official text, this is high-stakes for the US audience
Ferry durations/existence of fast options on all three Balearic legs are LOW CONFIDENCE — must be checked against current Trasmediterránea/Baleària timetables before writing
Hospital billing typical costs are unverified order-of-magnitude guesses only — should not be published as numbers without a source, or must stay qualitative
Barcelona's second annual local holiday (beyond La Mercè) could not be confidently named — needs the current city council decree
